claims.text: NbTaTiV is a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The BCC phase of NbTaTiV remains stable at temperatures up to 900°C.
NbTaTiV exhibits significant lattice distortion arising from atomic-size disparity.
A conventional BCC comparator can have similar yield strength to NbTaTiV while having lower atomic-size mismatch and lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion causes <111>{110} edge-dislocation cores to deviate from their neutral planes.
Deviation of edge-dislocation cores from their neutral planes produces a wavy dislocation structure.
Compositional fluctuations contribute to the formation of wavy dislocation lines.
Wavy dislocation configurations restrict dislocation glide and mobility at high temperatures.
Restricted dislocation glide promotes localized strain hardening.
Reduced dislocation mobility governs the high-temperature plastic-strain behavior of the refractory high-entropy alloy.
Restriction of dislocation glide reduces the high-temperature plastic-strain rate.
Restriction of dislocation glide and the associated strain hardening improve high-temperature toughness.
A high-lattice-distortion alloy will have a lower high-temperature plastic-strain rate than a conventional BCC baseline with minimal lattice distortion.
A high-lattice-distortion alloy will have greater high-temperature fracture toughness than the conventional BCC baseline.
The high-entropy alloy will contain a more irregular, wavy dislocation arrangement than the straighter arrangement expected in the conventional BCC baseline.
In situ neutron diffraction can reveal the relative waviness or core configuration of dislocations in the compared alloys.
The proposed mechanism applies when high-temperature plasticity occurs primarily through edge-dislocation processes in a single-phase refractory BCC alloy.
The proposed mechanism is not expected to govern behavior when phase transformations, grain-boundary sliding, diffusional creep, or other deformation modes dominate.
